comments.body:
It's possible to trigger this behavior without metaprogramming and without metavariables.

#13366 (a draft currently) has fixes to `Level.normalize` to ensure the result is in normal form.

(I'm considering `Level.equiv` to be orthogonal, and that the issue being reported here is effectively that you currently need to do `u.normalize.normalize` to make sure the level is actually normalized.)

comments.body:
Following [kmill’s distinction above](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues/12747#issuecomment-4225608216) between normalization producing a normal form and general completeness of level equality, I have a declaration-level reproduction of the first case in this issue. It may help clarify whether the corresponding C++ kernel normalization path is covered by #13366.

The definition declares universe parameters `u, v` and has these relevant fields:

```lean
value := Expr.sort (Level.imax u (Level.succ v))
type  := Expr.sort (Level.succ (Level.max u (Level.succ v)))
```

The exact [Lab-generated artifact in lean4export format](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/5d6e41fa85dfe215570e95adb549254b0c426956/corpus/generated/universe-imax-right-succ.ndjson) reaches kernel type checking through Arena’s official importer using Lean 4.33.0 (`d8b18978322de05a8f3dba51ef03cf5461676c17`) and is rejected:

```text
(kernel) declaration type mismatch, 'universeIMaxRightSucc' has type
  Type (imax u (v + 1))
but it is expected to have type
  Type (max u (v + 1))
```

[Raw replay output](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/5d6e41fa85dfe215570e95adb549254b0c426956/results/research/conditional-validation-contracts/cvc-4-conditional/run-0002/attempts/03/stderr).

Inferring the type of the supplied sort introduces an outer successor. Reading the C++ normalizer gives the following two-step behavior:

```text
L                       = succ (imax u (succ v))
normalize L             = succ (max u (succ v))
normalize (normalize L)  = max (succ u) (succ (succ v))
```

The declared type’s level normalizes directly to the last expression. The first normalization of `L` therefore leaves a result that changes on a second normalization, with a concrete consequence for the kernel’s comparison of these sort types through `is_equivalent`.

I also replayed the same bytes through Nanoda at `6ae1f0cd962f081f6c423454c5da729d841236a7`. For the two completed candidate/control pairs, the results are:

| Value level | Declared type level | Lean 4.33.0 | Nanoda |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max u (succ v)` | `succ (max u (succ v))` | accept | accept |
| `imax u (succ v)` | `succ (max u (succ v))` | reject | accept |
| `imax u 0` | `succ 0` | accept | accept |
| `imax u 0` | `succ u` | reject | reject |

Both level columns describe the argument of an `Expr.sort`. In particular, `imax u 0` is valid and denotes zero; the final row’s declared type fails to match the inferred type when `u > 0`. Nanoda accepts the right-successor declaration while distinguishing the two zero cases. [Fixed-artifact comparison and source mapping](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/5d6e41fa85dfe215570e95adb549254b0c426956/results/research/conditional-validation-contracts/cvc-4-conditional/report.md).

At master commit `c40679c304a1f8324981783c12275e109b051349`, [`src/kernel/level.cpp`](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/c40679c304a1f8324981783c12275e109b051349/src/kernel/level.cpp#L454-L521) is byte-for-byte identical to the [tested Lean 4.33.0 revision](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/d8b18978322de05a8f3dba51ef03cf5461676c17/src/kernel/level.cpp#L454-L521). The [sort-equality path](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/c40679c304a1f8324981783c12275e109b051349/src/kernel/type_checker.cpp#L781-L812) still reaches `is_equivalent`. This is a source comparison; I have not replayed the artifact on that master build.

In the PR diffs I inspected:

- [#13366](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/13366/files), at head `293afe9`, includes a Lean-side regression for `(imax u (v+1)) + 3`, but does not change `src/kernel/level.cpp`.
- [#14356](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/14356/files), at head `67730bd`, changes both implementations, addressing `max (succ u) 1` on the kernel side and `imax 1 u = u` on the Lean side. Those changes appear separate from the outer-offset case above.
- [#15050](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/15050), merged as `c40679c`, adds `leanchecker --from-export file.ndjson`, providing a route for a follow-up replay of this artifact.

<details>
<summary>Additional conditional semantic evidence</summary>

Separately, I checked a bridge from an independently defined Nat semantics for this small universe fragment to Lean4Lean’s positional universe model and its checked comparator results. The fixed right-successor example satisfies the named model under seven explicitly recorded assumptions, including Lean/Lean4Lean helper and runtime correspondence assumptions. This does not verify Nanoda, the C++ kernel, or arbitrary-byte importing.

The [checked proof](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/5d6e41fa85dfe215570e95adb549254b0c426956/results/research/conditional-validation-contracts/cvc-a7-repair-1/run-0002/attempts/03/CVC2Proof.lean), [assumption audit and scope](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/5d6e41fa85dfe215570e95adb549254b0c426956/results/research/conditional-validation-contracts/cvc-a7-repair-1/report.md), and [raw transitive axiom report](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/5d6e41fa85dfe215570e95adb549254b0c426956/results/research/conditional-validation-contracts/cvc-a7-repair-1/run-0002/attempts/03/stdout) are available for inspection.

</details>

Is the C++ normalization case intended to be covered by a pending change, or would this exact declaration be useful as a focused kernel regression? If useful, I’d be happy to submit a small regression PR; I can also work on the corresponding kernel fix once the preferred implementation direction relative to #13366/#14356 is clear.

My observation is limited to conservative rejection in this bounded case; I am not making a kernel soundness claim.

*This comment was drafted and reviewed with AI assistance from the Astra model.*
